He directed the company's finances and international retail expansion. long_biography.plain_text:
A silk screen built on a Pimlico kitchen table gave Bernard Ashley the practical role in the business he formed with Laura Ashley. Her patterns supplied the aesthetic; his engineering turned hand printing into continuous production. He relocated the machinery to rural mid-Wales, where the company created local factory work while its textiles and clothing reached international shops.

After Laura died, Ashley floated the company and pursued rapid overseas expansion under his chairmanship. The programme strained production, and delayed stock was followed by losses and repeated management conflict. He surrendered executive duties, then watched outside investment dilute family control until the Ashley connection ended in 2001.
